what: The comparison for Tipline: the same deck, wall, program and two 46.46 g towers, but the ballast heights are exchanged. Eight red plates rise 60.8 mm in one tower and descend 60.8 mm in the other. The green tower now has the high ballast, the orange tower the low ballast. Mass and base contact are unchanged; only the centre of mass moves.
try: Import tipline-swapped.ldr afresh in Robot Lab, place programs/tipline.bw in the Code tab, choose ⇦ To blocks and press Run.
Predict before running: which colour will tip first now?

Watch each base against the deck. Tipping is the tower rotating relative to the deck; sliding is the base moving downhill while the tower stays upright. A later lean against the yellow wall is a different event.
why: A block on a slope tips when the vertical line through its centre of mass passes outside the edge of its base, at tan θ = half-width / height of the centre of mass. It slides when tan θ exceeds the friction coefficient. Raising the ballast raises the centre of mass and lowers the tipping angle below the sliding angle; lowering it does the opposite. Swapping the ballast must therefore swap the outcomes between the lanes.
matters: The same comparison decides whether a loaded truck slides or rolls over on a slope, and why tall shelves and cranes carry their ballast low.
question: Both towers weigh the same and stand on the same base. Why does one tip and the other slide when the deck tilts?
answer: Their centres of mass sit at different heights. High ballast makes the tipping angle smaller than the sliding angle, so that tower tips first, near 15°; low ballast makes the tipping angle larger, so the tower slides first, near 22°. In the supplied native recordings the swapped scene gives 14.98° and 22.13°, the same as the main scene within 0.002°.
further: Use tan θ_tip = b / h to estimate the centre-of-mass height of the high-ballast tower from its tipping angle and its base half-width.
Estimate the friction coefficient from the sliding angle (μ ≈ tan 22°).
What happens if you raise the ballast of both towers?
formula: Tipping: tan θ_tip = b / h (b = half the base width downhill, h = centre-of-mass height). Sliding: tan θ_slide = μ. Whichever angle is smaller happens first.
